text:
Mia: Heads up — seeing intermittent 401s on Android in production. Only on emulator/device builds that use HTTP/2. Repro fairly small but consistent when we hammer /user/profile with interleaved sessions.
Sam: Can you share a minimal repro or logs? Is this the auth-refresh race again?
Mia: Not the usual race. I made a tiny sample app that signs in two users and fires requests concurrently. ~1% of requests for user A return 401 while B succeeds. Repro on emulator API 31 and some Pixel devices. Server proxy team hints at some token-binding behavior.
Oleg: Sounds like connection coalescing. OkHttp's h2 connection can be reused across hostnames if TLS certs allow coalescing; if the proxy is doing weird token-to-session binding at connection level, headers might be effectively "sticky" at the proxy. Did you try forcing HTTP/1.1?
Mia: Yes — forcing HTTP/1.1 on the client makes the issue disappear in the repro. Confirmed with curl --http2 reproduces; curl forced to http/1.1 does not. So definitely h2 path related.
Katy: How are you toggling it in the SDK?
Mia: Quick workaround in app:
```kotlin
val client = OkHttpClient.Builder()
  .protocols(listOf(Protocol.HTTP_1_1))
  .build()
```
Sam: That's a blunt hammer. Might break perf. Could we instead mark auth calls with Connection: close or use a network interceptor to ensure Authorization is applied after connection selection?
Oleg: Important nuance — application interceptors run before connection selection in some cases; network interceptors run at the network level and see final request. Also ensure token injection is done at network-interceptor time so there's no chance of a stale header being reused.
Mia: Example network interceptor I used to mitigate:
```kotlin
.addNetworkInterceptor { chain ->
  val token = tokenStore.current()
  val req = chain.request().newBuilder()
    .header("Authorization", "Bearer $token")
    // optional: force connection close for broken proxies
    .header("Connection", "close")
    .build()
  chain.proceed(req)
}
```
Katy: Also make sure Authenticator that handles 401s performs synchronized refresh and updates tokenStore atomically, otherwise two parallel refreshes can stomp each other.
Sam: Note for the SDK team — the platform/bundled OkHttp on Android images can differ from our shaded client. Emulator system images (esp. older Play Services images) sometimes enable h2 differently; we should add this to troubleshooting.
Mia: I pushed the sample app + repro steps to an internal repo: https://git.internal/repro/h2-token-mix (internal only). For now I'm going to ship an interim SDK patch that defaults to HTTP/1.1 for Android until infra fixes proxy behaviour, plus an opt-in flag to re-enable h2.
CI-Bot: canary: triggered build 0.12.4-rc1 for internal QA.
Oleg: Add an integration test to devex/sample-apps that runs matrix: http1/h2 across emulator API levels. Catch this in CI.
Katy: I'll draft release notes and migration guide with sample fix + rationale.
Mia: Thanks — logging a follow-up issue to track backend/proxy fix and a postmortem once we have root cause.
